question: Is the >50 ms renderer long-task background on the synthetic fixture caused by the number of sidebar sessions, or by opening a long transcript?
method: Same probe, same 180 KB-per-transcript fixture, only TF0423_SESSION_COUNT differs. Both runs use the committed after build (08744fac dist).
finding: The long-task background scales with sidebar session count, not with the transcript size of the opened session: 20 sessions -> 0 long tasks on open and 1 in the idle control; 333 sessions -> 8 on open and 6 idle. Opening one 180 KB transcript adds no distinct long-task class; the cost is the 333-row sidebar itself.
implication: TF-0423 acceptance item 3 ("opening a long session must not produce a renderer long task over 50 ms") is unattainable while the sidebar mounts/updates hundreds of rows on this forced-software-rendering host. The remaining work is sidebar render containment/virtualization, which is outside the transcript-read and label-budget fix shipped in 08744fac.
